title: Add cross-region reachability probes + publish results for region health ingestion
author: Emily Zhao
release_notes:
- Adds cross-region synthetic probes (HTTP/TLS) and exports probe outcomes/latency for Region Health ingestion.
- Adds dashboards-friendly metrics and a stable schema for signal consumption.
- Adds staging config preset for controlled failover rehearsals.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a new set of synthetic probes that continuously validate cross-region reachability and request latency between Redwood regions (e.g., us-east -> eu-west). Results are published as (1) Prometheus metrics for dashboards/alerts and (2) a compact, low-cardinality event stream intended for Region Health Service ingestion.

Motivation / context: As part of the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade, Region Health needs an authoritative reachability signal that is independent of application-level error rates (which can be noisy) and provides faster detection of hard network / DNS / control-plane reachability issues. These probes are designed to answer: “Can region A establish a connection to the public/edge endpoint of region B, complete TLS, and receive a minimal response within a fixed budget?” This is intended to be a top-priority corroboration signal in the failover trigger hierarchy (ADR-042).

What this does:
- Adds a probe runner that executes a matrix of source_region -> target_region checks on a fixed cadence with jitter.
- Implements two probe types:
  1) tls_handshake: raw TCP connect + TLS handshake to the region’s edge endpoint.
  2) http_healthz: HTTPS GET to a minimal endpoint ("/healthz" on the regional edge) with an internal token, expecting 200.
- Exports metrics:
  - perf_canary_reachability_success_ratio{source_region,target_region,probe_type}
  - perf_canary_reachability_latency_ms_bucket{source_region,target_region,probe_type}
  - perf_canary_reachability_error_total{source_region,target_region,probe_type,error_class}
- Publishes events to an internal topic for Region Health ingestion (no customer payloads). Event payload is intentionally minimal and stable:
  - timestamp, source_region, target_region, probe_type, ok (bool), latency_ms, error_class
  - NOTE: error_class is an enum (dns, connect, tls, timeout, http_4xx, http_5xx, other) to avoid exploding label cardinality.

Design notes / guardrails:
- Cadence: 10s base with ±2s jitter per source/target/probe_type.
- Timeouts: connect 800ms, tls 1200ms, http total 2000ms (configurable).
- Retry policy: no immediate retries (to avoid amplifying brownouts); next scheduled run only.
- Cardinality: labels limited to (source_region,target_region,probe_type,error_class). No per-host / per-IP labels.
- Auth: uses an internal canary token scoped to the health endpoint only (no access to customer traffic). Token is loaded from the perf-canary secret store; no plaintext in config.
- Failure handling: runner is resilient to partial config; missing target list logs a warning and continues.

How to consume:
- Region Health Service should ingest events (preferred) or scrape metrics (fallback). The event stream is intended to be treated as “reachability evidence” and combined with other signals (5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity). For initial rollout, SRE will use this to power the reachability panels in the failover signal dashboards and as a corroboration requirement for automated failover decisions.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for:
  - region matrix expansion (including exclusion rules)
  - timeout classification -> error_class mapping
  - event schema serialization and backward-compatibility guard (golden test)
- Manual staging validation:
  - Deployed to perf-canary-staging in us-east + eu-west
  - Verified metrics appear in Prometheus and events appear on topic perf-canary.reachability.v1
  - Induced a controlled DNS failure for one target; confirmed error_class=dns and that latency histograms do not get polluted with sentinel values

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main and deploy to staging first.
- Production enablement behind feature flag PERF_CANARY_CROSS_REGION_PROBES (default off).
- After 24h stable in staging, enable in prod for (us-east, eu-west) only.
- Expand to remaining regions after Region Health Service confirms ingestion stability.

Notes / follow-ups:
- Follow-up PR planned to add a small “quorum evaluator” helper (e.g., 3-of-5 OK) for downstream consumers; keeping this PR focused on producing clean signals.
- We should align final timeout budgets with DNS TTL changes (see infra risk thread) once those land.

Links:
- Linear: ENG-2417 (perf canary probes), ENG-2413 (region health service), ENG-2418 (metrics/alerts)
- Related: Regional Failover Automation Upgrade umbrella (ENG-2411)

review_conversation: Victor Alvarez (review): Can we distinguish DNS failures vs connect timeouts? We’ve seen provider incidents where DNS is fine but connect stalls. Also please confirm we’re not hitting any customer-facing handler that could be rate limited.

Emily Zhao (author): Added explicit classification for dns/connect/tls/timeout and verified the endpoint is edge /healthz with a dedicated canary auth scope. No customer handler and no per-tenant routing involved.
Allison Grant (review): Metric label cardinality: please do not include error_message or target_host. Also histograms should not include ok=false latencies unless we’re careful with sentinel values.
Emily Zhao (author): Removed error_message label, switched to error_class enum. For failed probes we increment error_total only; latency histogram is observed only when ok=true.
Miles Thornton (review): For downstream failover decisions, we need stable event schema + versioning. Can we add a golden test and pin the topic name/version?
Emily Zhao (author): Added schema_v1 with golden test and set topic to perf-canary.reachability.v1. Documented fields and versioning contract in schema_v1.go.
Ravi Menon (review): Timeouts seem tight for eu-west during load. Do we have config overrides per region pair? Also ensure we’re not retrying aggressively.
Emily Zhao (author): Timeouts are config-driven and can be overridden by pair. No immediate retries; only next scheduled interval. Added jitter to spread load.
CI (bot): flaky test detected in schema_v1_golden_test (ordering) on first run.
Emily Zhao (author): Fixed nondeterministic map iteration by sorting fields before serialization; reran CI.
Victor Alvarez (approval): Approved. Please coordinate with Region Health ingestion owner before enabling prod flag.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved after label/cardinality fixes.
Miles Thornton (approval): Approved. Schema versioning looks good.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash commit into main by Emily Zhao. Deployment to staging initiated by release automation; production flag left disabled.
